info.title: Lied API
info.description: Sheet-music management REST API. Authenticate with a bearer token from `POST /v1/tokens` or a session cookie from `/admin/login`.

post.description:
Returns the plaintext token exactly once; the server stores only an
argon2id hash. Use the token as the password in
`Authorization: Basic base64(username:token)` for WebDAV clients.

201.description: App password created; token shown once

delete.description:
Revoking does not end any web session or invalidate any bearer token —
the three auth paths are independent.

post.description:
The request body must be `multipart/form-data` with a single part that
carries a recognised `Content-Type` (see the format table in docs/design.md).
The file is streamed directly to MinIO — server memory per upload is a
fixed chunk buffer, not proportional to file size.

An arrangement whose full score already holds `LIED_MAX_FILES_PER_VOICE`
live files refuses a new one with `409`; replace an existing file instead.

413.description: Upload exceeds the configured size limit

put.description:
The replacement must carry the same `Content-Type` as the original. A
format change requires uploading a new file instead. The MinIO object key
is unchanged; MinIO versioning captures the content history.

413.description: Upload exceeds the configured size limit

delete.description:
The MinIO object is retained; the DB row is hidden from listings. The
object can be recovered via a future admin hard-delete / undelete path.

numbering (a program's labels are its positions). Narrowing `numberWidth`

post.summary: Assign a player to many parts of a collection at once
post.description:
Each created row is an ordinary part assignment. Pairs the player already
holds are reported in `alreadyHeld`, not duplicated, so the same request can
be re-sent after pieces are added. If any pair no longer names a live piece
of this collection and a live voice of its arrangement that is still the
requested part (`instrumentId` + `partNumber`), nothing is written and the
response is `409` — preview again. Audit rows are written in the same
transaction as the assignments.

get.summary: Preview assigning a player to one part across a collection
get.description:
A voice matches when its primary instrument (the first of its
`instrumentIds`) is `instrumentId` and it has the same `partNumber` (both
absent counts as the same); the other instruments of a doubling part do
not make it that instrument's part. Each piece reports one outcome: `assign`,
`alreadyHeld`, `noMatch` (with the piece's voices for that instrument as
`candidates`), `ambiguous` (more than one match, listed in `candidates`), or
`removed`. `alsoHolds` lists other parts of the same piece the player
already holds — a conflict that is reported, not refused.

parameters.name: instrumentId
parameters.description: The part's instrument: matched against each voice's primary instrument.

parameters.name: partNumber
parameters.description:
The part number (the `1` of "Trumpet in Bb 1"). Omit to match voices
that carry no part number, such as Timpani or Harp.

200.description: What would happen to each piece

get.description:
Staff see every voice of every piece. A `musician` with `is_principal = true`
sees only their own section — the voices whose instrument is in their
`principal_instrument_ids` — which is the one non-staff-facing view in this
tree. Everyone else gets `403`.

200.description: Coverage report; scoped to the caller's section when they are a principal

post.summary: Add a musician to a voice on a collection item
post.description:
**Adds a player; it does not replace one.** A part is played by as many
musicians as the section has (issue #53), so this is a `POST` that appends
to the assignments collection: always `201`, and `409` when the same person
is added to the same voice twice.

There is no `If-Match` here because nothing is being overwritten. Removing a
player is `DELETE` by assignment id and changing distribution state is
`PATCH` by assignment id; both keep their optimistic-concurrency contract.

post.description:
This changes the numbers printed in the players' folders, so it applies
only the preview the client showed: a `previewToken` from a collection
that has changed since is a 409, and the client previews again.

Programs only: a standing collection's order follows its labels, so it
answers 409; relabel, swap or renumber its pieces instead.
A program has no sections (409); a start another section has is a 409.

post.description: Authenticate via an existing session cookie (common path: logged into admin UI) or via `username`+`password` in the body (programmatic path). Hence the security list: anonymous (with credentials in the body) or a `session` cookie; a bearer token is not accepted here. The cookie path is a cookie-authenticated write, so it must carry the session's CSRF token (the `lied_csrf` cookie) in the `HX-CSRF` header; the username/password path needs no header. The returned token is valid for the configured lifetime (default 30 days).

403.description: Session cookie presented without a matching `HX-CSRF` header

AppPasswordSummary.description:
Wire representation of an `app_password` row. Never carries `hash` or
the plaintext token — only metadata, per docs/design.md's "shown ONCE on
creation" rule.

assignments.description:
The `(collectionItemId, voiceId)` pairs to assign — normally the
`assign` entries of a preview. At least one.

instrumentId.description:
The part being assigned — the same `instrumentId` / `partNumber` the
preview was asked for. Every pair must still be that part, or the
request is refused with `409`: a voice renumbered or re-instrumented
since the preview is no longer the part the client was shown.

partNumber.description: Omitted or `null` for a part without a number.

alreadyHeld.description: Submitted pairs the player already held; left unchanged.

AttachTagRequest.description: Request body for attaching a tag to an arrangement.

Collection.description:
Wire representation of a `collection` row. `camelCase` per docs/design.md's
JSON-casing convention.

numberWidth.description:
Digits in the WebDAV folder names of its pieces (`007-…` or
`0007-…`), and so the highest label: 999 or 9999.

label.description:
The number players are called by: `12`, or `12a` for a piece slipped
in later. In a program it is always `position` as text. Display it.

position.description: Running order, 1..n over the live items; order a list by it.

oneOf.description:
The section the piece's number falls into (the one with the greatest
start at or below it); `null` before the first section, in a
collection without sections, and always in a program.

arrangementRemoved.description:
`true` when the referenced arrangement is soft-deleted — render it as
"[removed]" with the slug, not as a live entry.

CollectionItemView.description:
A collection item plus its referenced arrangement's display info, so a
soft-deleted ("removed") arrangement is surfaced rather than dropped.

startsAt.description:
The first number the section covers; it runs until the next
section's start.

Conflict.description:
One musician holding several voices in the same piece.

Legal and sometimes necessary — sections get juggled by who turns up — but
nobody plays two parts at once, so a piece covered this way is not as ready
as its tallies suggest. Reported, never prevented.

content.description: The annotation itself, e.g. "bar 112: cut to the coda".

name.description:
Human-readable label (e.g. "iPad in rehearsal room"). Must be unique
per user.

token.description:
Plaintext token shown exactly once at creation.

Format: `lied_<base64url(32 bytes)>`. Store it now — it cannot be
retrieved again.

CreateAppPasswordResponse.description:
Response from `POST /v1/app-passwords` — includes the plaintext token
shown exactly once.

CreateArrangementRequest.description: Request body for creating an arrangement.

CreateCollectionRequest.description: Request body for creating a collection.

numberWidth.description:
Digits in the WebDAV folder names, and so the highest label: `3`
(up to 999, the default) or `4` (up to 9999, for a large book).

type.description:
`program` (a concert: numbers are positions) or `standing` (a
Marschbuch: numbers are labels that keep their gaps).

CreateItemRequest.description: Request body for adding an item to a collection.

label.description:
Standing collections only: the piece's number, `12` or `12a`. Must
be a free number below the highest, the highest + 1 (the default),
or a letter after a number in use; anything else is a 400, a taken
label a 409.

position.description:
Programs only: where the piece goes, 1..n+1 (default: the end); the
pieces from there on move down one.

CreateSectionRequest.description: Request body for adding a section.

startsAt.description:
The first number the section covers, 1 up to the collection's
width (999 or 9999). It may lie past the highest number (a new
section after the others), or inside the numbers in use, dividing
the folder; no number changes either way.

CreateTagRequest.description: Request body for creating a tag.

CreateVoiceRequest.description: Request body for creating a voice.

instrumentIds.description:
The instruments this part is read on, primary first: at least one,
none twice.

partNumber.description:
Which part of its instrument this is: at least 1, or `null` for a part
with no number (Timpani, Harp).

**Omitting it is not the same as `null`.** An omitted `partNumber` is
guessed from the name ("Trumpet in Bb 1" → 1; combined parts such as
"Horn 1 & 3" get none).

FileResponse.description: Metadata about a stored file (score or voice).

GlobalAnnotation.description:
Wire representation of an annotation, with its author's display name so a
list can be rendered without a lookup per row.

ItemCoverage.description: One piece of the collection, with its voices and their tallies.

arrangementRemoved.description:
The arrangement was removed from the catalogue. The piece still holds
its slot in the programme (hide-with-references), but its voices are
**not** counted as required — a slot that has lost its music is a
problem to see, not a gap to chase.

conflicts.description: Musicians holding more than one voice in *this* piece.

label.description: The piece's number, as players are called by it (`12`, `12a`).

players.description:
Players: how many **distinct people** are assigned across those parts,
and how many of them have acknowledged everything they hold. A different
question with a different denominator from the part counts, so the two
must be labelled wherever they are shown.

Distinct people, not assignment rows: somebody holding two voices of
this piece is one musician who cannot be in two places — which is what
`conflicts` says — and counting them twice would inflate a section that
is in fact short-handed.

position.description: The piece's place in the running order.

required.description:
Parts: how many voices this piece needs, and how many have anybody on
them.

ItemSection.description: The section an item falls into, as much as a client needs to show it.

LabelChoices.description: The labels a new piece of a standing collection can take.

gaps.description: Free numbers below the highest one of their section, ascending.

sections.description:
Each section's next number, by start; empty without sections. The
numbers before the first section appear as an entry without a
section when the first section does not start at 1.

suggested.description:
The highest number + 1 (`1` in an empty collection): the default
when a piece is added without a label. `null` when it would not fit
the collection's width.

MeMembership.description: One of the caller's memberships, with its organization.

MeOrganization.description:
The organization a membership belongs to, as much as a client needs to
show and enter it.

memberships.description:
Every organization the caller is a member of, ordered by organization
name; empty for a guest or a system admin without memberships. Not
paginated: one entry per organization the caller belongs to.

org.description:
Optional active org id to scope the token to (docs/design.md JWT claims:
`org`, nullable). Not validated against Membership in this item —
org-scoping enforcement is a later authorization concern; minting
just records the claim.

password.description: User's password. Required when no session cookie is present.

username.description: Login identifier. Required when no session cookie is present.

Outcome.description: What bulk assignment would do with one piece.

PlanItem.description: The plan for one piece of the collection.

alsoHolds.description:
For [`Outcome::Assign`]: other voices of this piece the player already
holds. Not an error — sections get juggled — but one person cannot play
two parts at once, so it is surfaced next to the assignment.

candidates.description:
For [`Outcome::Ambiguous`]: the matching voices. For
[`Outcome::NoMatch`]: every voice of the same instrument in the piece.

label.description: The piece's number, as players are called by it (`12`, `12a`).

position.description: The piece's place in the running order.

Player.description:
One musician playing one part, and how far their assignment has got.

`notified_at` stays separate from `acknowledged_at` because "assigned but
nobody has told them" and "told, but no reply" are different problems with
different fixes.

items.description: One entry per live piece of the collection, in running order.

ProblemDetails.description:
RFC 7807 Problem Details — the body of every `/v1` error response
(`application/problem+json`).

This is a documentation-only schema twin of the serialization produced by
`AppError::into_response`; it does **not** replace the production error
type in `lied/src/error.rs`.

detail.description: Human-readable detail about this specific occurrence.

errors.description:
Field-level validation errors (`garde` failures), present on `400`.

Shape: `{ "fieldName": ["message1", …] }`.

status.description: HTTP status code (mirrors the response status).

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the error kind.

RenumberChange.description: One piece's number before and after a renumber.

RenumberCollectionRequest.description: Request body for applying a renumber.

RenumberPreview.description: What a renumber would do, and the token that applies exactly that.

changes.description:
Every live piece, in order, with its label now and after the
renumber (equal where it does not change).

previewToken.description:
Pass it back to apply this preview; it no longer matches once the
collection's pieces, labels or sections change.

sectionChanges.description: Every section, in order, with its start now and after the renumber.

changes.description: Every piece, in order, with its label before and after.

sectionChanges.description: Every section, in order, with its start before and after.

ReorderRequest.description: Request body for reordering a collection's items.

orderedIds.description: The item IDs in their new order; reassigned positions `1..=n`.

Role.description:
`Membership.role` (CLAUDE.md: text + CHECK, not a native PG enum — see
Implementation conventions). Ordered loosely by seniority for readability
only; the database is the source of truth for valid values via CHECK.

SectionLabelChoice.description: The next number one section offers.

full.description:
`true` when `next` is `null`: take a gap, a letter label (`75a`), or
renumber.

next.description:
The section's start while it holds no piece, else the number after
its highest. `null` when the section is full (that number is the
next section's start) or past the collection's width.

sectionId.description: `null` for the numbers before the first section.

SectionRenumberChange.description: One section's start before and after a renumber.

SwapItemRequest.description: Request body for swapping two pieces.

withItemId.description: The other piece, in the same collection.

UndeleteItemRequest.description: Optional request body for restoring a removed item.

label.description:
Standing collections only: the label to restore the piece under when
its old one is taken, under the same rule as adding.

UpdateAnnotationRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH …/annotations/{annotationId}`: every field optional, and an
omitted one is left unchanged. Unknown fields are refused, so a misspelled
key is a 400 rather than a silent no-op.

UpdateArrangementRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH …/arrangements/{arrangementId}`: a partial update. An
omitted field is kept; `null` clears a nullable field. `title` and
`status` are required by the model, so they can be changed but not cleared.

UpdateAssignmentRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH .../assignments/{assignmentId}` — sets or clears
`notifiedAt`/`acknowledgedAt`. The notification/acknowledgement
*workflow* is deferred (docs/design.md phase-1 cut), but the fields are
settable now. A partial update: an omitted field is kept, `null` clears it.

UpdateCollectionRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH …/collections/{collectionId}`: a partial update; an omitted
field is kept.

numberWidth.description:
`3` or `4`. Widening renames every WebDAV folder; narrowing is a 409
while a label would not fit.

type.description:
`program` or `standing`. Program → standing keeps the numbers as
labels; standing → program closes the gaps.

UpdateItemRequest.description:
Request body for moving an item: a partial update like every `PATCH`, so
`{}` (or the item's current place) changes nothing.

label.description:
Standing collections only: the new label, under the same rule as
adding (the piece's own current label does not count against it).

position.description: Programs only: the new position, 1..n; the pieces in between shift.

UpdateMemberRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/orgs/{orgId}/members/{memberId}`: a partial
update. An omitted field is kept; none of these fields is nullable, so
`null` is the same as omitting it (send `[]` to empty an instrument list).

UpdateOrgRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/orgs/{orgId}`: a partial update; an omitted
`name` is kept. The slug never changes here (slug rename is its own,
admin-gated operation).

UpdateSectionRequest.description:
Request body for changing a section: a partial update like every
`PATCH`, so `{}` changes nothing.

startsAt.description: A new first number. The pieces around it regroup; no number changes.

UpdateTagRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH …/tags/{tagId}`: a partial update. An omitted field
is kept; `kind: null` clears the kind.

UpdateVoiceRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH …/voices/{voiceId}`: a partial update. An omitted
field is kept — in particular an omitted `partNumber` is never re-guessed
from a new name, and a client that predates the field cannot erase it.
Send `partNumber: null` to clear it.

instrumentIds.description:
Replaces the whole list when sent (primary first, at least one, none
twice); omitted keeps it.

UpdateWorkRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/works/{workId}`: a partial update. An omitted
field is kept; `composer: null` clears the composer.

UploadForm.description:
Multipart upload body: a single `file` part with a `filename` and a
recognised `Content-Type`.

Documented here as the OpenAPI `requestBody` schema for upload/replace
endpoints; the actual extraction is done by axum's [`Multipart`] extractor.

User.description:
Wire representation of a `user` row. `password_hash` is intentionally
never included — this type must never leak it via any `/v1` response.

VoiceCoverage.description:
One voice of one piece and everyone playing it.

Acknowledgement is deliberately **not** reduced to a per-voice flag: a
section where two of three players have replied is neither "rehearsed" nor
"not rehearsed", and collapsing it would hide which. The ratio is rendered
instead (issue #53).

VoiceRef.description: A voice as the plan reports it.

instrumentIds.description:
The instruments this part is read on, in order and never empty; the
first is the primary ("Flute 2 / Piccolo" is `[flute, piccolo]`).

Work.description:
Wire representation of a `work` row. `camelCase` per docs/design.md's JSON-
casing convention.

session.name: lied_session
session.description: Session cookie set by `/admin/login`. State-changing requests (anything but GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE) authenticated by this cookie must also send the session's CSRF token, read from the `lied_csrf` cookie, in the `HX-CSRF` request header; without it they are refused with 403 (`https://lied/errors/csrf-token-invalid`). Any cookie-authenticated `/v1` response sets `lied_csrf` when the client lacks the current token, so one request (a GET will do) before the first write is enough. The cookie is used only when the request has no `Authorization` header: a bearer request is authenticated by its token alone and needs no CSRF header, and any other `Authorization` scheme is a 401.
